messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bad behavior of sampler
parts:
Running in the current develop branch (well, current as of
this AM), this model (also attached)

data {
int N;
real y[N];
}
parameters {
real lambda1;
real lambda2;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}
transformed parameters {
real mu;
mu <- lambda1 + lambda2;
}
model {
lambda1 ~ normal(0,10);
lambda2 ~ normal(0,10);
y ~ normal(mu, sigma);
}

with 100 unit normal simulated data points (also attached)
spins out of control with this call

./weakprior sample data file=sim-data.R id=1 output file=weakprior-1.csv random seed=55555

I don't understand why there's a problem --- there's no prior on sigma, but I'd
have thought the posterior would be proper.

...
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the
sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is 0:0, but must be > 0!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the
sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.
...


I believe that variate is for the prior on lambda_1 or lambda_2.

- Bob

There's definition a different behavior in develop now verses develop a few merges ago.  The biggest difference is that many more sigma=0 errors are spat out -- this could be because
the sampler is actually exploring deep into - log(sigma) and sigma is underflowing, it could be because the check itself was changed, or it could be that the change from catching only
std::domain_error to std::exception opened up the error message flood gates (although that wouldn't make much sense here as the message should be output for either).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bad behavior of sampler
parts:
On 2/7/14, 5:16 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> There's definition a different behavior in develop now verses develop a few merges ago.
I know!

> The biggest difference is that
> many more sigma=0 errors are spat out --
Exactly.

> this could be because
> the sampler is actually exploring deep into - log(sigma) and sigma is underflowing,

You mean because the target acceptance rate is higher?
I get the same problem setting adapt delta=0.65 as it was
before.

Or is there some other reason it'd be exploring deeper? Is it the initialization
at the random starting point that's the issue? If I set init=0, the problem goes
away.

WTF?

Did the initial step size routine change, or is it just that we're
now starting from the parameter values rather than init=0?

> it could be because the check itself
> was changed,

I don't think this has been changed at all. We're hitting boundary
errors in the distributions, which have been there all along.

> or it could be that the change from catching only
> std::domain_error to std::exception opened up the error message flood gates (although that wouldn't make much sense here
> as the message should be output for either).

That also seems unlikely. It's still domain errors that
are being caught. The overflow to -infinity still gets
transformed back to 0, then hits the domain error that's getting
reported.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bad behavior of sampler
parts:
Got it! And it's a good lesson in exception handling.

If you look at:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/commit/ce0d4157aa0a214c3830a9ac7057f1156276b954

you'll see that

try {
z.V = - stan::model::log_prob_grad<true,true>(_model, z.q, z.g, _err_stream);
} catch (std::domain_error e) {
this->_write_error_msg(_err_stream, e);
z.V = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
}

was replaced with

try {
stan::model::gradient<true, true>(_model, z.q, z.V, z.g, _err_stream);
} catch (std::domain_error e) {
this->_write_error_msg(_err_stream, e);
z.V = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
}
z.V *= -1;

The z.V *= -1 should have gone inside the try, not outside.
That is, it should only get called when the gradient there succeeded.

I'll create an issue, fix it on a branch and create a pull request
ASAP.

- Bob
